# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#
# Cadence perft corpus fixture.
#
# Provenance and diagnostic explanation: docs/testing/perft.md
#
# The two leading pipe tables supply standard-position FENs and the
# human-readable summary that the integrity tests cross-check against the
# standard-perft TSV block. Named fenced blocks retain their original info
# strings; fields in TSV blocks are separated by literal tab characters.
# An empty summary-table cell means no value is recorded at that depth. The
# cell keeps its spaces: a `||` with nothing between the pipes would be one
# column short, because the parser trims repeated pipes from the row's ends.
| # | Position | FEN |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | startpos | `rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1` |
| 2 | Kiwipete | `r3k2r/p1ppqpb1/bn2pnp1/3PN3/1p2P3/2N2Q1p/PPPBBPPP/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1` |
| 3 | pos3 | `8/2p5/3p4/KP5r/1R3p1k/8/4P1P1/8 w - - 0 1` |
| 4 | pos4 | `r3k2r/Pppp1ppp/1b3nbN/nP6/BBP1P3/q4N2/Pp1P2PP/R2Q1RK1 w kq - 0 1` |
| 5 | pos5 | `rnbq1k1r/pp1Pbppp/2p5/8/2B5/8/PPP1NnPP/RNBQK2R w KQ - 1 8` |
| 6 | pos6 | `r4rk1/1pp1qppp/p1np1n2/2b1p1B1/2B1P1b1/P1NP1N2/1PP1QPPP/R4RK1 w - - 0 10` |

| Position | d1 | d2 | d3 | d4 | d5 | d6 | d7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| startpos | 20 | 400 | 8,902 | 197,281 | 4,865,609 | 119,060,324 | 3,195,901,860 |
| Kiwipete | 48 | 2,039 | 97,862 | 4,085,603 | 193,690,690 | 8,031,647,685 |   |
| pos3 | 14 | 191 | 2,812 | 43,238 | 674,624 | 11,030,083 | 178,633,661 |
| pos4 | 6 | 264 | 9,467 | 422,333 | 15,833,292 | 706,045,033 |   |
| pos5 | 44 | 1,486 | 62,379 | 2,103,487 | 89,941,194 | 3,048,196,529 |   |
| pos6 | 46 | 2,079 | 89,890 | 3,894,594 | 164,075,551 | 6,923,051,137 |   |

```text ambiguity-proof
FEN:   6k1/8/8/8/8/8/8/5K1R w H - 0 1
legal: f1e1 f1e2 f1f2 f1g1 f1g2 f1h1 h1g1 h1h2 h1h3 h1h4 h1h5 h1h6 h1h7 h1h8
                        ^^^^        ^^^^
                   quiet king move   castling (king takes rook)

FEN:   5k1r/8/8/8/8/8/8/6K1 b h - 0 1
legal: f8e7 f8e8 f8f7 f8g7 f8g8 f8h8 h8g8 h8h1 h8h2 h8h3 h8h4 h8h5 h8h6 h8h7
                        ^^^^        ^^^^
                   quiet king move   castling (king takes rook)
```

```tsv edge-cases
8/8/8/4k3/8/8/8/4R1K1 b - - 0 1	6	102	562	9777	King may not retreat ALONG the checking ray. The king must be removed from the occupancy when testing its own destination squares, or it blocks the checking ray beyond itself and e4/e6 test as safe. A naive generator yields 8 here instead of 6.
4k3/8/8/8/3Pp3/8/8/4R1K1 b - d3 0 1	6	82	574	8889	En passant, VERTICAL pin on the capturing pawn: e4xd3 e.p. is ILLEGAL. A standard pin mask DOES catch this one.
8/8/8/K2pP2r/8/8/8/7k w - d6 0 1	6	78	528	8288	En passant, HORIZONTAL double-vacate: e5xd6 e.p. is ILLEGAL. NEITHER pawn is individually pinned - remove only one and the other still blocks. A pin mask does NOT catch this. Requires an explicit occupancy-modified attack test.
8/8/8/2pP4/8/8/8/K6k w - c6 0 1	5	19	110	688	POSITIVE CONTROL: d5xc6 e.p. is LEGAL. Guards against an over-eager ep filter.
8/8/1k6/2b5/2pP4/8/5K2/8 b - d3 0 1	15	126	1928	13931	POSITIVE CONTROL with a bishop on the board: c4xd3 e.p. is LEGAL.
4k3/8/5N2/8/8/8/8/4RK2 b - - 0 1	3	69	214	4782	DOUBLE CHECK (slider + knight). Black Ke8 is checked by Re1 and Nf6 at once. No capture of one checker and no interposition can resolve both, so generation must restrict to king moves the moment checkers.count() >= 2. All three legal moves are king moves. This is the ONLY position in the corpus that exercises that branch.
2r3K1/4P3/8/8/8/8/8/k7 w - - 0 1	7	107	1031	15495	UNDERPROMOTION RESOLVING CHECK BY INTERPOSITION. White Kg8 is checked along rank 8 by Rc8; e7-e8 promotes onto the checking ray and blocks. All FOUR promotion pieces block equally well. A generator that emits only queen promotions when in check, or that computes block squares without expanding promotion pieces, returns 4 instead of 7.
7k/P7/8/8/8/8/8/K7 w - - 0 1	7	19	213	1103	PROMOTION GIVING CHECK. a7-a8=Q and a7-a8=R check Kh8 along rank 8; =B and =N do not. The check is delivered by a piece that did not exist in the parent position, so anything caching attack sets by piece type across make_move is wrong here.
2r4k/1P6/8/8/8/8/8/K7 w - - 0 1	11	104	1012	12433	PROMOTION-CAPTURE GIVING CHECK. b7xc8=Q/R check Kh8 along rank 8. The quiet b7-b8 promotion does NOT check, because the rook on c8 is still there to block: the capture and the check are the same move, and removing the blocker is what enables the check. Promotion-capture is also the only move type reaching the DirtyPieces maximum of 3 entries.
8/8/8/4k3/3Pp3/8/8/7K b - d3 0 1	8	29	215	1234	EN PASSANT AS A CHECK EVASION. Black Ke5 is checked by the pawn that just played d2-d4. e4xd3 e.p. removes the checker, but its DESTINATION (d3) is neither the checker's square (d4) nor on BETWEEN[e5][d4], which is empty because the two are adjacent. A generator whose evasion target mask is `checker | BETWEEN[king][checker]` misses it and returns 7.
4k3/8/8/2PpP3/8/8/8/4K3 w - d6 0 2	9	47	376	2321	TWO PAWNS CAPTURING THE SAME EP SQUARE. Both c5xd6 and e5xd6 are legal. An implementation written against the false invariant "at most one ep capture per position" generates one of them and returns 8.
```

```text edge-case-moves
  (6)  e5d4 e5d5 e5d6 e5f4 e5f5 e5f6
       -- note the ABSENCE of e5e4 and e5e6

  (6)  e4e3 e8d7 e8d8 e8e7 e8f7 e8f8
       -- note the ABSENCE of e4d3

  (6)  a5a4 a5a6 a5b4 a5b5 a5b6 e5e6
       -- note the ABSENCE of e5d6

  (5)  a1a2 a1b1 a1b2 d5c6 d5d6
       -- d5c6 IS present

8/8/1k6/2b5/2pP4/8/5K2/8 b - d3 0 1
  (15) b6a5 b6a6 b6a7 b6b5 b6b7 b6c6 b6c7 c4c3 c4d3
       c5a3 c5b4 c5d4 c5d6 c5e7 c5f8
       -- c4d3 IS present

4k3/8/5N2/8/8/8/8/4RK2 b - - 0 1
  (3)  e8d8 e8f7 e8f8
       -- king moves ONLY. Note the ABSENCE of any capture or interposition;
          e8e7 is illegal (Re1) and e8d7 is illegal (Nf6)

2r3K1/4P3/8/8/8/8/8/k7 w - - 0 1
  (7)  e7e8b e7e8n e7e8q e7e8r g8f7 g8g7 g8h7
       -- ALL FOUR promotions are legal blocks; g8f8 and g8h8 are illegal
          (f8 is on the checking ray, h8 is behind the king on it)

7k/P7/8/8/8/8/8/K7 w - - 0 1
  (7)  a1a2 a1b1 a1b2 a7a8b a7a8n a7a8q a7a8r
       -- a7a8q and a7a8r give check; a7a8b and a7a8n do not

2r4k/1P6/8/8/8/8/8/K7 w - - 0 1
  (11) a1a2 a1b1 a1b2 b7b8b b7b8n b7b8q b7b8r b7c8b b7c8n b7c8q b7c8r
       -- b7c8q and b7c8r give check; the quiet b7b8 promotions do not

8/8/8/4k3/3Pp3/8/8/7K b - d3 0 1
  (8)  e4d3 e5d4 e5d5 e5d6 e5e6 e5f4 e5f5 e5f6
       -- e4d3 IS present, and it is an EP CAPTURE resolving a check

4k3/8/8/2PpP3/8/8/8/4K3 w - d6 0 2
  (9)  c5c6 c5d6 e1d1 e1d2 e1e2 e1f1 e1f2 e5d6 e5e6
       -- BOTH c5d6 and e5d6 are present
```

```tsv ep-evasion
8/8/8/4k3/3Pp3/8/8/7K b - d3 0 1	e4d3	d4		The checker is the pawn on d4 and it is adjacent to the king on e5, so BETWEEN is empty and the whole mask is {d4}. The legal evasion e4xd3 e.p. lands on d3, outside the mask, because en passant captures a piece that is not on the destination square.
```

```text ep-rule
occ2 = (occ ^ from ^ captured_pawn) | to
if slider attacks on our king under occ2 exist -> reject
```

```tsv castling-rights-capture
rkr5/8/8/8/8/8/8/Q5K1 w ca - 0 1	a1a8	ca	c	24	392	8475	163366	OPPONENT'S RIGHT DIES. A queen captures the rook on its ORIGIN square. No white right is involved, so this isolates update_mask[to].
rkr5/8/8/8/8/8/8/RKR5 w CAca - 0 1	a1a8	CAca	Cc	20	328	6855	138584	ROOK-TAKES-ROOK. Both rights die in one move: White's because its rook left a1 (update_mask[from]), Black's because its rook was captured on a8 (update_mask[to]). This is the case the single branchless AND exists for.
```

```tsv fen-notation
rkr5/8/8/8/8/8/8/RKR5 w CAca - 0 1	rkr5/8/8/8/8/8/8/RKR5 w KQkq - 0 1	20	328	6855	138584	King between its rooks but NO rook on the h- or a-file edge beyond them. X-FEN spells this KQkq, where K denotes the OUTERMOST rook on the king's side (c1), not the h-file. A parser that reads K as 'the h1 rook' finds nothing there and silently drops the right.
rkr3r1/8/8/8/8/8/8/RKR3R1 w CAca - 0 1	rkr3r1/8/8/8/8/8/8/RKR3R1 w CQcq - 0 1	29	710	20488	561661	THE FALLBACK. An extra rook on g1/g8 sits outside the castling rook, so K would be ambiguous and X-FEN is FORCED to name the file. Note the mixed spelling: the queenside keeps Q because a1 IS outermost. Shredder never mixes.
```

```tsv move-capacity
R6R/3Q4/1Q4Q1/4Q3/2Q4Q/Q4Q2/pp1Q4/kBNN1KB1 w - - 0 1	218	99	19073	85043	MAXIMUM LEGAL MOVE COUNT. 218 moves, the known maximum. Black is close to stalemate, so d2 is only 99 -- the width of this position is entirely at the root, which is exactly what is wanted.
```
